decisions.reason: As a newly launched classic handle line that fits the firm's core assortment and supports broad project coverage, it is unlikely to be withdrawn so soon without negative market signals.
This handle family is close to the established business and helps serve different design and budget needs, so a large German supplier would normally retain it in the portfolio.
Although a single design variant can be pruned more easily than a full family, it still aligns with the firm's design-led hardware offering and is too new for an early exit to be likely.
This product is adjacent to the core door-handle business and likely contributes to range depth for architects and planners, making withdrawal within a year relatively unlikely.
A multi-model lever-handle family strengthens the firm's system breadth and specification options, which are central to its competitive position, so it should be kept.
The electronic access system is a flagship product in the firm's stated strategic direction toward digital building organization, so management would be very unlikely to remove it.
